thread:
anna_support: FYI a customer (jMorris) reports EU users suddenly hitting us-west pop, huge tail latency and intermittent 401s. Billing alert triggered.
anna_support: Sample request-id: req_0a1b2c3d; user IPs: 185.47.92.14, 2a02:6b8::feed
customer_jMorris: Confirmed — started ~2026-03-15 08:10 UTC. Some requests auth ok, others 401, looks like requests bouncing between eu-central and us-west.
mike_sre: Can you paste a few dig/traceroute from affected client? Also the auth logs from gateway for that req-id.
anna_support: Asked customer for traceroute and dig; they sent back:

```
$ dig +short @9.9.9.9 api.redwood.example.com
13.227.14.3    <-- us-west
93.184.216.34  <-- eu? (cached stale)
```

and traceroute shows path to 13.227.14.3

lucy_net: That looks like resolver-level split view / stale geoDB answer or ISP ECS stripping. Ask them to run `dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.example.com` and `dig @8.8.8.8 +short +edns=0` to compare.
customer_jMorris: Ran those, results:

```
@1.1.1.1 -> 52.29.10.11  (eu-answers)
@8.8.8.8 -> 13.227.14.3  (us-west)
```

customer_jMorris: Their corporate resolver is doing weird caching.
mike_sre: Two likely vectors: 1) our GeoIP/anycast pool returned mixed set due to recent geodb patch; 2) upstream resolver (ISP) is returning stale/incorrect cached mapping because of EDNS stripping or NAT. The 401s could be token issued for eu-pop but validated in us-pop (session affinity mismatch).
evan_prodops: deploy-bot: last geoip sync job status?
deploy-bot: geoip-sync-job finished 2026-03-15T07:58:21Z, uploaded geodb v2026.03.15.07 to S3, propagated to edge in ~2m. :white_check_mark:
lucy_net: Hmm propagation claim is fine, but some ISPs still have old answers cached (TTL) or rewrite EDNS. Need to check our authoritative DNS TTL and EDNS behavior. What's TTL on those records?
mike_sre: From authoritative:

```
$ dig @ns1.redwood.example.com api.redwood.example.com A +noall +answer
api.redwood.example.com. 60 IN A 52.29.10.11
api.redwood.example.com. 60 IN A 13.227.14.3
```

TTL is 60s — short. But if ISP caches longer or ignores TTL, they'll serve stale.
anna_support: Customer also sent auth logs (redacted):

```
[2026-03-15T08:12:11Z] req_0a1b2c3d token=tok_xyz validated at us-west -> 200
[2026-03-15T08:12:13Z] req_0a1b2c3d token=tok_xyz validated at eu-central -> 401
```

mike_sre: That indicates token issuance/validation race across regions. Our token binding uses `region` claim when issued by some backends depending on which pop served issuance request.
lucy_net: Immediate mitigation: 1) Add a fallback route to prefer eu endpoints for EU CIDR ranges in smart routing config for this customer. 2) Increase token grace acceptance across regions for short window (~5s).
evan_prodops: Are those changes low-risk? We can push a routing policy override scoped to the customer account only.
mike_sre: Routing override fine. Token grace change touches auth — requires quick regression but doable with feature flag.
anna_support: Proposed action list for customer impact window:
- Ask customer to flush their corporate resolver or use 1.1.1.1 as temporary workaround.
- Apply a customer-scoped routing rule to prefer eu-pop (quick rollbackable).
- Enable token grace period feature-flag for 10m window.
- Continue monitoring billing alerts and auth error rate.

lucy_net: Also create a short repro: simulate upstream resolver that strips EDNS and caches old A records. I can run a local stub and test.

```
# reproduce with dig
dig @<local-stub> api.redwood.example.com +tcp +noedns
```

mike_sre: I'll add a synthetic check: query major public resolvers and compare geo answers (1.1.1.1, 8.8.8.8, 9.9.9.9) and run traces to chosen IPs. If mismatch > 20% for EU traffic, we trigger routing override automatically.
evan_prodops: Rolling customer-scoped routing override now, will monitor.

deploy-bot: route-override:created account=jMorris scope=eu-prefer id=route_8421 by=evan_prodops

anna_support: Customer confirms improvement after switching to 1.1.1.1 — latency back to normal, auth 401s dropped.
customer_jMorris: Thanks team, clearing our corp resolver cache fixed it for now. Will monitor.
mike_sre: Follow-ups:
- Investigate ISP-level caches rewriting TTLs/EDNS. Open ticket with their network.
- Add guard in auth validator to accept tokens from recently-propagated regions for few seconds.
- Add resolver-consistency check to our onboarding docs and runbook.

lucy_net: I'll schedule a deeper postmortem if we see recurrence. For now marking P1->P2 because customer is back to normal. :relieved:
anna_support: Closing loop with customer and documenting steps in the ticket. Thanks all! :thumbsup:
